title: Card Grading Price (2026)
verdict: The card grading price at AGS is $18 per card, the same for every card, and bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards drop to $15.
What you pay depends on three things: how many cards, how fast, and whether the grader charges by value. One card at AGS is $18. Thirty are $15 each. The faster bulk tiers add $5 or $15 a card.

sections.note: Each company's own listed terms, checked November 18, 2026. Confirm before you ship.

sections.h: What one card costs to grade
p: Grading fees only, at each company's listed entry price. Shipping, insurance and supplies are extra everywhere.
list: AGS: $18 (1 x $18, no minimum), 20 business days or less, subgrades included.
CGC Economy: $13 (Bulk needs 10 cards), 25 working days.
Beckett Base: $14.95, or $17.95 with subgrades, 45 business days or more.
PSA Value: $32.99, before any declared-value upcharge.

sections.h: What the fee does not cover
list: Shipping to the grader, tracked and insured.
Return shipping and insurance. AGS calculates it at checkout.
Supplies: penny sleeves, semi-rigid card savers, a box.
At some graders, a membership to reach the cheapest tier, a fee for subgrades, or a charge if the card is valued above the tier.

ranking.fit: Anyone with a mix of card values who does not want to pay by declared value.
ranking.lacks: Bulk pricing needs 30 cards. CGC's needs 10.
ranking.note: $18 flat with no minimum, or $15 a card from 30 TCG cards. Code AGSNEW20 takes 20% off a first order, and nothing is charged until the cards are graded.

ranking.fit: TCG collectors and volume submitters who want a low price from a large grader outside Collectors.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want subgrades printed on the label from an old name.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: Sellers who want the widest buyer pool and the highest resale prices.
ranking.lacks: One grade, no subgrades, and fees that rise with declared value.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want one flat $15 price and a 14-day turnaround.
ranking.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less on most cards.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters who mainly want cards protected and labeled.
ranking.lacks: The lowest prices need 25 cards, or 100.

why: The price does not move with the card. AGS charges $18 per card whatever it is worth, with bulk tiers from $15 at 30 cards. PSA and SGC price by declared value and CGC caps each tier by card value, so a card that turns out to be worth more can cost more to grade.

The wait is short because the grading step is short. AGS lists 20 business days or less on its standard service, 10 and 5 business days on the faster tiers, and same-day grading on request for urgent cards.
Nothing is locked in. No minimum order, no membership, no contract, and payment is taken when the cards are graded. A first order gets 20% off with code AGSNEW20.

faq.q: What is the card grading price?
faq.a: Most entry tiers cost $10 to $50 a card in November 2026. AGS is $18 with subgrades and a report included.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: When do you pay for grading?
faq.a: AGS charges when the cards are graded and ready to ship, not when you submit.

faq.q: Is it worth grading a low-value card?
faq.a: Only if grading lifts the price by more than the fee plus shipping, or if you want the card protected and documented. At $10 to $18 a card the math works on far more cards than at $50.

faq.q: Is there a discount on a first AGS order?
faq.a: Yes. AGS lists code AGSNEW20 for 20% off a first grading order.
